label: COMMUNICATION

cover.headline: Bring it up *before it builds*
cover.sub: 5 ways to raise a small thing while it’s still small.

points.heading: Small things grow when unsaid
points.body: A minor irritation kept quiet often comes out later, bigger and sharper.
points.panel: If it’s still on your mind after a day, it’s worth mentioning.

points.heading: Pick a calm moment
points.body: Not when you’re both tired, hungry, or rushing out the door.
points.panel: “Do you have a few minutes later to talk about something small?”

points.heading: Keep it about one thing
points.body: Stay with this one issue, not the full history.
points.panel: “I want to talk about the dishes, just that.”

points.heading: Say how it affects you
points.body: Your feelings are easier to hear than a judgment of him.
points.panel: “When it piles up, I feel like I’m doing it alone.”

points.heading: End with a small ask
points.body: Give him something clear he can do.

close.save: Save this for the next small thing.

caption:
Many couples don’t fight about big issues. They fight about small ones that were left unsaid until they weren’t small anymore.

Raising things early, calmly, and one at a time keeps them manageable. Here are five ways to say the small thing while it’s still small, so it doesn’t turn into the big one later.
